question: By how many percentage points did acid washing lower the ash content (Aad) of the lignite used for co-pyrolysis with sawdust, and by what share of its original value?
expect: 7.02 to 1.48: 5.54 points, about 79% of the original (78.9%) (Table 1)
rendered:
Document: [Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass]

Page 1: The original lignite coal (LC, original) had an ash content (Aad) of 7.02 wt%.

Page 2: The acid-washed lignite coal (LC) had an ash content (Aad) of 1.53 wt%.

The acid washing lowered the ash content (Aad) of the lignite by 7.02 - 1.53 = 5.49 wt%.

The share of the original ash content that was lowered by acid washing is (5.49 / 7.02) * 100% ≈ 78.3%.
